churn_resistance.rationale: Data access, config and env are excellently centralized, so an upgrade or an API move is cheap. But the client/server boundary is untyped on both sides (any everywhere), the pokemon payload ships far more than it renders, and 404 is a data flag rather than a status — three things that guarantee rework when requirements or payloads change.

findings.issue: useFetch<any> throws away the response types Nuxt infers from the server routes; the whole client/server contract is any-typed.
findings.suggestion: Drop the explicit <any> and let Nuxt infer the handler return types; export shared DTO interfaces from server/utils/pokeapi.ts and use them for the page-data builders.

findings.issue: /api/pokemon/:name serializes move rows for every version group (hundreds of rows for Pikachu) while the page renders one group.
findings.suggestion: Accept ?game= in the handler and return only the selected group's tables, or move grouping server-side; the client already round-trips the game param.

findings.issue: Upstream fetches have no timeout or AbortController; a slow PokeAPI request hangs the page render forever, and the promise cache never invalidates on success.
findings.suggestion: Pass AbortSignal.timeout(10000) to fetch and cache with a TTL (or keyed on a data-version) so live-data changes eventually surface.

findings.issue: Not-found is modeled as in-band data (notFound: true) rather than an HTTP 404 via createError, so caching, prefetching and SEO semantics can't be improved without touching every page.
findings.suggestion: throw createError({ statusCode: 404 }) from the server handlers and render an error.vue page.

findings.issue: definePageMeta({}) is a no-op macro call; dead boilerplate that a reviewer must think about.
findings.suggestion: Delete it, or use it for what it's for (e.g. definePageMeta({ name: 'pokedex' })).

findings.issue: pageUrl/searchString hand-roll query-string building and percent-encoding.
findings.suggestion: Use router.resolve({ path: '/', query }).fullPath (or URLSearchParams) so encoding rules live with the router.

findings.issue: decodeURIComponent(getRouterParam(...)) can double-decode a param the router already decoded.
findings.suggestion: Trust getRouterParam's value (or add a comment/test documenting the router's decoding behavior) — PokéAPI names never contain % today, which is exactly why this will surprise someone later.

findings.issue: process.env.API_BASE_URL read directly instead of via Nuxt's runtimeConfig.
findings.suggestion: Add runtimeConfig: { apiBaseUrl: 'http://localhost:9000' } and read it with useRuntimeConfig(event), the Nuxt-blessed place for environment-driven config.

summary: This is a clean, current Nuxt 4.6.3 app with a single dependency, centralized upstream data access, and the framework's modern primitives (useFetch with reactive URLs, useHead, Nitro server routes), so an upgrade would touch very few files. The main debts are at the client/server boundary: every page discards inferred response types, the Pokémon payload ships all version groups' move tables at once, and 404 is modeled as data rather than a status. Those are cheap to fix now and expensive to fix once behavior depends on them.

apis.replacement: defineHandler (or a plain function) only under h3 v2 / Nitro v3, which is still beta; the installed stack is h3 1.15 / Nitro 2.13 (h3.dev/migration, nitro.build/docs/migration)
useRuntimeConfig(event) with a runtimeConfig entry — the Nuxt-blessed pattern for environment-driven config
